Clark & Hadfield — Regulatory Markets for AI Safety (2019)

Jack Clark and Gillian Hadfield propose global regulatory markets: governments set outcomes and license private regulators, and AI companies must buy regulatory services from one of them. They test the idea against credit rating agencies, the Boeing 737 MAX, medical-device single audits and UK legal services, and sketch a prototype for adversarial robustness in commercial drones. The Oggy Assessment asks whether government can measure outcomes well enough to oversee the overseers, and what the model means for runtime oversight of AI systems.
